stories.title: Latest U.S. Strikes on Qeshm Island Hit Fishermen Who Clung to Wreckage for Hours
stories.text: TEHRAN, Iran—On the morning of October 31, Mehrzad Panjeh and his brother Mehran were fishing in the Strait of Hormuz off of Qeshm Island when a drone struck the water near their boat. The blast set the boat on fire and threw Mehran into the sea. Mehrzad, whose knee was broken in the attack, could only watch from the burning deck as his brother struggled in the water. Their relatives Mohammad Panjeh and his son Mahmoud were also hit as they fished in a nearby boat. Their boat broke apart, leaving the two clinging to the floating wreckage for hours. The four had come to check on baited hooks left in the water between the town of Souza and the village of Mesen on the Qeshm’s southern coast, a method known locally as ghollab-e entezari, or “waiting hooks.” “We were doing our usual work, just what we were doing as fishermen for years,” Mehrzad Panjeh told Drop Site News. “We never thought it would come to that.” The four fishermen were wounded, but miraculously survived. The attack, at around 11:30 a.m. about 18 nautical miles off Mesen , was one of at least three strikes in Iran’s southern waters over four days. stories.title: PopInfo Weekly: Crickets, cash, and conflicts
stories.text: Last week, Democrats on the House Judiciary Committee released a report about President Trump’s alleged relationship with Jeffrey Epstein. The report includes a new allegation that Trump raped a Swiss model at a pageant in 1993. The majority of media outlets ignored the new allegation. A Popular Information review of coverage by 25 major media outlets found that 20 did not publish any substantive reporting on the allegation. A Popular Information analysis of Federal Election Commission (FEC) data revealed that $1.4 billion in midterm spending came from non-profit organizations that do not have to disclose their donors. Spending from dark money organizations was over six times higher this election cycle than in 2018. Separately, a large amount of money came from a small handful of known donors. The top 10 known donors during the midterm election cycle donated over $1 billion, including $436 million from Elon Musk. Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner has simultaneously represented the U.S. in high-stakes negotiations involving Ukraine, Iran, and Gaza while collecting untold millions in fees from Middle Eastern governments through his private equity firm. stories.title: The Real Architect of the Iran Mess
stories.text: Adm. Brad Cooper on new podcast “Inside CENTCOM” Not accepting a dime in corporate ad money allows me to be genuinely independent; but it also means I’m ENTIRELY dependent on readers like you to survive. The timing couldn’t be more hilarious. The entire country just voted against his Iran war, and there’s Cooper, the architect, grinning and chatting up his workout routine, love of french fries and basketball. Asked about Operation Epic Fury, he says only that “I just couldn’t be prouder” and how even amidst the war he guards the “sanctity” of his workouts. Considering that Cooper never bothered to make keeping the Strait of Hormuz open an objective of the war — which sent oil prices soaring — maybe he should’ve spent less time working out. stories.title: Encircled and Besieged, Taiz City Is a Refuge for Displaced Yemenis Fleeing War
stories.text: Residents in Taiz city crowding around a bakery to buy bread, as families now prefer store-bought bread to preserve their remaining household cooking gas which is in short supply. TAIZ CITY, Yemen—Hana Bagash never imagined that, one day, she would have to flee Taiz, the city in southwestern Yemen where she was born and raised. But in early October, as fighting intensified around the city between Saudi-backed government forces and Ansarallah, the 40-year-old mother of four decided it was no longer safe for herself and her children and decided to flee. “On October 2, I coordinated with my sister in the town of Al-Turbah, who rented a house for us. I took my children and fled the city,” Bagash told Drop Site News. Her husband is currently working in Djibouti, so she had to make the move alone. Al-Turbah, located in Taiz governorate some 70 kilometers south of Taiz city, was safe when she arrived. Just two days later, Ansarallah (also known as the Houthis) took control of the town following the withdrawal of government forces. stories.author: The Lever team
stories.title: The Blue Wave Might Have Washed Away Progressives’ Leverage
stories.text: 💡 This article first appeared in The Lever’s flagship newsletter, Lever Daily . On Tuesday, Democrats not only managed to take back both the House and Senate but also secured larger majorities than many observers had dreamed was possible. In the House, Democrats are currently projected to secure a 42-seat majority, while in the Senate, which some expected to remain under Republican control, Democrats have at least a four-seat majority. But for the progressive insurgents aiming to exert their newfound power, could these numbers prove to be a double-edged sword? Now that Democrats have the House, minority leader Hakeem Jeffries has officially announced his bid for speaker, despite his lagging approval ratings and new disclosures about his corporate backers . To win, Jeffries needs a simple majority vote in the House. Just a few weeks ago, when Democrats were projected to win only a slim majority, that vote would have required Jeffries to rally the entire caucus behind him. Now, the margins are wide enough that, as it stands, Jeffries is expected to “ cruise” to victory .
